text:
Detroit hosts San Jose tonight with the better underlying numbers. The model projects 3.44 expected goals for DET and 2.86 for SJS. At five on five, the Red Wings have taken 53% of the expected goals this season to the Sharks' 41%. San Jose creates 2.57 expected goals per 60 and allows 3.82, while Detroit sits at 3.29 and 3.15. The special teams matchup favors DET too: its power play creates 0.92 expected goals a game, and SJS's penalty kill allows 1.05, which ranks 31st in chances allowed. Detroit takes 4.4 penalties a game, which keeps handing the other side power plays.

The recent form tells the same story. DET is 2-1-2 in its last five with 51% of the expected goals, and it has won the chance battle in three of those. SJS is 2-3-0 with 39%, and it has not won the chance battle in any of the five, even though two of its games went to overtime or a shootout wins. The Red Wings are better than their record, a -4 goal difference on +1.0 expected, because finishing has cost them 7.4 goals against the chances.

In net, the projected goalies are Yaroslav Askarov for SJS (-1.4 goals saved above expected this season, -19.4 last season) and John Gibson for DET (-3.14 this season, +10.11 last season). For players, DeBrincat has a 43% chance to score and Larkin 37%, while Celebrini leads San Jose at 38% and a 74% chance at a point. Lucas Raymond has 4 points in seven games against about 6.6 expected, and his chances are still there.
